questions.subject: Paper-I · General English
questions.stem:
Passage: The Industrial Revolution, which began in Britain in the late 18th century, was powered largely by coal. Steam engines, fuelled by coal, drove factories, railways, and ships, transforming economies and societies. The demand for coal led to the expansion of mining operations across Europe and America. However, the social cost was high, with poor working conditions, child labour, and environmental pollution. The legacy of the Industrial Revolution continues to influence modern industrial practices and environmental policies. Today, many former mining regions are being revitalised through diversification and clean energy initiatives.

Former mining regions are being revitalised through:
questions.solution: Diversification and clean energy initiatives

questions.subject: Paper-I · General English
questions.stem:
Passage: India's energy demand is projected to grow at 3-4% annually over the next decade. While coal remains the dominant source, accounting for about 55% of installed capacity, renewable energy is expanding rapidly. Solar power capacity has grown from just 2.6 GW in 2014 to over 70 GW in 2024. Wind power contributes another 45 GW. The government's Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for solar manufacturing aims to reduce dependence on imports. Nuclear power, with 7.5 GW capacity, and hydropower, with 47 GW, are other important components of India's energy portfolio.

Coal accounts for about what percentage of India's installed capacity?

questions.subject: Paper-I · General English
questions.stem:
Passage: Coal is the most abundant fossil fuel in India and plays a crucial role in the country's energy mix. India has the fourth-largest coal reserves in the world, with an estimated 344 billion tonnes. Coal India Limited (CIL) is the largest coal-producing company globally, accounting for about 82% of India's coal output. However, concerns about environmental degradation and climate change have prompted a shift towards cleaner energy sources like solar and wind power. The government has set a target of achieving 500 GW of renewable energy capacity by 2030.

According to the passage, India has the ____ largest coal reserves in the world.
questions.solution: fourth

questions.subject: Paper-I · General English
questions.stem:
Passage: Underground mining is one of the most hazardous occupations in the world. The primary risks include roof falls, gas explosions, flooding, and ventilation failures. In India, the Mines Act of 1952 and the Coal Mines Regulations of 2017 govern safety standards. Modern technology has significantly improved mine safety through real-time monitoring systems, gas detectors, and automated equipment. Despite these advances, safety remains a critical concern, and regular training programs are mandatory for all mine workers. The introduction of continuous miners and longwall mining methods has increased both productivity and safety.

The Coal Mines Regulations were enacted in:

questions.subject: Paper-I · General English
questions.stem:
Passage: The Gondwana coal fields of eastern India contain the country's best quality coal. These fields stretch across Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha, and Chhattisgarh. The coal found here is primarily bituminous, which has high calorific value and low ash content. In contrast, the Tertiary coal fields of northeastern India contain lignite and sub-bituminous coal. Coal grading is based on ash content, with higher grades having lower ash percentages. Washeries are used to reduce ash content and improve coal quality before it is supplied to power plants and industries.

Coal grading is primarily based on:
questions.solution: Ash content

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A graptolite rhabdosome grows in which direction from the first zooid (sicula), and how is stipe growth described?
options: Upward from the prosicula. Stipe growth is scandent or reclined, never branching
Random and variable. No fixed growth direction exists among the colonial graptoloids
From sicula (first zooid) downward. Stipe growth: scandent (graptoloid) or dendroid
Sideways from the initial bud. Stipe growth is planar and confined to a horizontal sheet
questions.solution: Graptolite: sicula → stipe growth. scandent: stipes merge (Monograptus). Dendroid: branching.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Ammonite zonation of sedimentary strata is chiefly used for which purpose?
questions.solution: Ammonites: rapid evolution, wide distribution. Excellent index fossils for Jurassic-Cretaceous marine rocks.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A P-wave travels at 6 km/s and arrives 20 s after the earthquake. The (approx.) distance to the source is:
questions.solution: distance = velocity × time = 6×20 = 120 km.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In a complete evaporite sequence, minerals appear from bottom to top in which order?
questions.solution: Evaporite: decreasing solubility upward. Ca-carbonate first, then Ca-sulfate (gypsum), NaCl (halite), KCl (potash).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What do the inclined layers of cross-bedding reveal about the depositional setting?
options: Randomly oriented, chaotic fabric with no preferred layer orientation
Strictly horizontal layers showing no inclination in any direction
Inclined layers within horizontal strata. Wind or water current direction
Vertically dipping layers formed by folding of originally horizontal strata
questions.solution: Cross-bedding: dune migration. Paleocurrent indicator.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Von Mises stress criterion predicts yielding when:
options: Second deviatoric stress invariant reaches critical value
Maximum principal stress attains the tensile yield strength
Resolved shear stress on the plane equals the cohesive strength
Differential stress drops to zero under hydrostatic pressure
questions.solution: Von Mises: √(J₂) = k. J₂ = second invariant of deviatoric stress. Smooth criterion, good for ductile metals.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which peridotite variety consists of more than 90% of the mineral olivine?
options: Rock with more than ninety percent quartz and minor feldspar
Rock with more than ninety percent pyroxene and no olivine
Rock with more than ninety percent plagioclase feldspar
questions.solution: Dunite: light green, massive. Altered to serpentinite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Pseudosection modeling constructs a thermodynamic phase diagram for which specified condition?
options: ACF diagram projected from quartz and fluid for a fixed bulk composition and a given metamorphic temperature
Petrogenetic grid of univariant reactions independent of bulk composition and valid for any rock type
Thermodynamic phase diagram for specific bulk composition. Perple_X, Theriak-Domino. Isopleths for P-T
AFM diagram valid for one bulk composition and one metamorphic pressure without isopleth contours
questions.solution: Pseudosection: modes + compositions of phases. Contours of T/P. Compare with natural assemblage.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) is computed using which two spectral bands of a sensor?
questions.solution: NDVI = (NIR - Red)/(NIR + Red). High = healthy vegetation.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Distinguish marine transgression from regression in terms of shoreline shift and the resulting stratal stacking pattern:
options: Both processes move the shoreline progressively landward over time
Transgression: landward shoreline shift (retrogradational). Regression: basinward (progradational)
Regression moves the shoreline landward while transgression moves it basinward, reversing the usual definitions
Transgression moves the shoreline basinward and regression moves it landward
questions.solution: Transgression: sea-level rise + sediment supply < accommodation.Ravinement surface.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A mineral specimen of mass 81 g has a volume of 20 cm³. Its specific gravity is about:
questions.solution: SG = mass/volume = 81/20 = 4.05.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Slate is the low-grade metamorphic product of:
questions.solution: Fine-grained shale metamorphoses to slate, with characteristic slaty cleavage.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The cleat system in coal refers to which type of naturally occurring fracture set?
options: Random fractures with no preferred orientation and irregular spacing distributed throughout the coal seam body
Joints inclined at high angles to the bedding planes of the coal seam itself
Bedding-plane partings along the depositional surfaces of the original coal seam
Natural fractures perpendicular to bedding. Face cleats (primary) and butt cleats (secondary)
questions.solution: Cleats: orthogonal system. Control permeability. Spacing: mm to m. Face cleats continuous.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Plate boundary triple junctions: RRR type (ridge-ridge-ridge):
options: Two plates converging while the third moves along a transform fault
All three plates converging toward a common central point
All three plates separating. Example: Azores, Afar
One ridge, one trench and one transform fault meeting at a single point
questions.solution: Triple junction: RRR stable (receding). TTT stable (subducting). RRR at Afar: Red Sea, Gulf of Aden, Rift.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The principle of isostasy states that the crust is balanced how upon the denser mantle?
options: Crust floats on denser mantle in gravitational equilibrium
The lithosphere remains fixed and rigid over geologic time
Mantle density varies randomly without any relation to relief
Continental crust and oceanic crust have identical densities
questions.solution: Airy: mountain roots. Pratt: lateral density. Glacial rebound confirms.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Conodont elements, which are phosphatic tooth-like structures, are now recognized as belonging to what kind of animal?
options: Arthropod with a mineralised carapace and calcite lens-bearing compound eyes
Mollusk whose aragonitic shell was progressively replaced by phosphate during burial
Annelid worm whose chitinous jaws were secreted as a fused feeding apparatus
questions.solution: Conodonts: primitive chordate. Elements used for biostratigraphy. CAI = thermal maturity.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Mass extinction events are identified by:
options: Sharp decrease in biodiversity in fossil record
A gradual steady decline spanning several periods
Uniform diversity levels across boundary strata
An abrupt increase in endemism and faunal provinciality
questions.solution: Mass extinction: >75% species loss in <1 Myr. 5 major events identified. Sharp drop in diversity in stratigraphic record.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Heavy minerals concentrated by flowing water in stream beds form a:
questions.solution: Placers (e.g. of gold, cassiterite) form where moving water sorts dense, durable grains.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In the samarium-neodymium radiometric system, the radioactive parent samarium-147 decays by alpha emission to produce which daughter isotope?
questions.solution: Sm-Nd dating: 147Sm → 143Nd. Half-life ~106 Ga. Good for mafic/ultramafic rocks. Less affected by metamorphism.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Isograd: line on map connecting points of same metamorphic grade. Defined by:
options: First appearance of index mineral (e.g., garnet, staurolite)
Last appearance of the index mineral in the same metamorphic zone
Boundary between two different rock types on the geological map
Constant abundance of one mineral throughout the metamorphic belt
questions.solution: Isograd: reaction isograd. Garnet-in, staurolite-in, kyanite-in. Maps P-T conditions.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Exsolution lamellae in feldspar indicate:
options: Rapid quenching of a volcanic glass
questions.solution: Exsolution: two feldspar phases separate on cooling. Perthite: K-feldspar + plagioclase lamellae. Indicates slow cooling.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the age, composition, and significance of the Peninsular Gneissic Complex of the Dharwar region?
options: Closepet Granite batholith that intrudes the E-W greenstone belts of Kolar
Cuddapah platform cover that unconformably overlies the older basement rocks
Banded gneissic complex in Dharwar. TTG composition. 3.4-3.0 Ga
Sargur supracrustal rocks that lie folded within the gneissic terrain of Mysore
questions.solution: Peninsular Gneiss: basement for Dharwar. Multiple deformation events. Migmatitic.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: To extract 15 m³ of coal, 45 m³ of overburden must be removed. The stripping ratio is:
questions.solution: Stripping ratio = overburden/coal = 45/15 = 3 : 1.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Ophiolite complexes are slices of oceanic lithosphere thrust onto continental margins. An ophiolite sequence consists of which units?
options: Continental lithosphere thrust beneath the oceanic crust forming a thick slab that descends to depths of several hundred kilometres
Volcanic arc crust accreted onto the continental margin during the closure of a back-arc basin
Sediments deposited in a continental rift basin recording progressive transgression
Oceanic lithosphere obducted onto continent. Harzburgite → layered gabbro → sheeted dike → pillow lava → pelagic sediment
questions.solution: Ophiolite: Oman, Troodos (Cyprus). Moho transition zone. SSZ (supra-subduction zone) ophiolite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which minerals are characteristic of the high-pressure, low-temperature blueschist facies?
options: Pyroxene, garnet, feldspar with no hydrous minerals at all
questions.solution: Blueschist: HP/LT subduction. Glaucophane: diagnostic blue amphibole. Jadeite: Na-pyroxene.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is shotcrete and how is it applied in underground construction?
options: Concrete cast in timber formwork and cured for twenty-eight days before any loading
Precast panels bolted onto the rock face with no bonding material at all
Sprayed concrete (dry or wet mix). Steel fiber reinforced. Applied to rock surface
Poured tremie concrete placed underwater through a tremie delivery pipe
questions.solution: Shotcrete: immediate support. Add accelerator. Wire mesh or fiber. 50-100mm thick.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Packer tests in boreholes are used to isolate and measure the permeability of:
options: Specific depth intervals in borehole for permeability measurement
The entire borehole so that the full saturated aquifer thickness is tested
Surface water bodies from the influence of the borehole test
Only the aquitard layers that bound the main aquifer under test
questions.solution: Packer test: inflatable packers seal interval. Pump or slug test in isolated zone.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Crystal twinning: contact twin vs penetration twin:
options: No difference. Contact and penetration twins are simply two names for the same intergrowth
Contact = interpenetrating. The two types share identical geometry at the junction
Contact: shared plane (mirror). Penetration: shared point (interpenetrating)
Same thing. Both twins form by the same interpenetrating growth mechanism
questions.solution: Contact: staurolite, gypsum. Penetration: fluorite, pyrite, garnet twins.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A mineral has passed through 2 half-lives of an isotope whose half-life is 1.3 (in the given time units). Its age is:
questions.solution: Age = number of half-lives × half-life = 2×1.3 = 2.6.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the chemical composition of dolomite, and how does it typically form?
options: CaCO3 — the same as calcite, forming inorganically from seawater
CaMg(CO3)2 — forms by Mg replacement of calcite
FeCO3 — iron carbonate formed under reducing diagenetic conditions
SiO2 — silica mineral formed by recrystallization of biogenic ooze
questions.solution: Dolomite: effervesces weakly in cold HCl. CaMg(CO3)2.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What geological setting gives rise to a mud volcano erupting mud and gas?
options: A normal volcanic eruption of molten lava and pyroclastic material rising from the deep mantle of the earth
Ejection of mud and gas from depth. Overpressured sediments. Often in accretionary wedges
An ordinary cold spring discharging mineral-poor surface water near the coast
A fault scarp formed purely by tectonic extension of the earth's crust at the surface
questions.solution: Mud volcano: methane, water, fine sediment. Onshore (Azerbaijan) and offshore. Cone-shaped.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which vegetation index performs better in high-biomass areas and incorporates blue along with red and near-infrared bands?
options: A simple two-band ratio of red and near-infrared reflectance values, identical to NDVI
Identical to NDVI but with atmospheric correction applied and no soil adjustment factor as well
Enhanced Vegetation Index. EVI = 2.5×(NIR-R)/(NIR+6R-7.5B+1). Better for high biomass
An index that requires no soil brightness adjustment factor in its calculation
questions.solution: EVI: reduces atmospheric and soil noise. For dense vegetation (Amazon). MODIS EVI product.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes sapping or spring erosion and the valley forms it produces?
options: Groundwater outflow → headward erosion. Box canyon, amphitheater valleys. Colorado Plateau
Erosion caused only by the overland flow of surface water during periods of heavy rainfall in the region
Erosion caused only by the action of wind on the land surface of the surrounding arid desert region of the world today
Erosion caused only by the action of moving glacier ice over the land surface lying below the glacier
questions.solution: Sapping: chemical weathering at spring outlets. Canyon head propagation. Piping erosion.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes isostasy and distinguishes the Airy and Pratt models of crustal equilibrium?
options: Isostasy involves only lateral variations in the density of the Earth's crustal rocks and nothing else at all whatsoever
Buoyant equilibrium of Earth's crust. Airy (variable root depth) vs Pratt (variable density)
Isostasy involves only lateral variations in the thickness of the Earth's crust and nothing else whatsoever
The Earth's crust is not in any kind of equilibrium at all in any region of the world today
questions.solution: Airy: mountains have deep roots (like iceberg). Pratt: density varies laterally. Flexural isostasy.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes the surface produced when ice-rich permafrost thaws?
options: Irregular surface from thawing of ice-rich permafrost. Subsidence, ponds
Landforms produced by wind erosion in arid desert regions of the world
Landforms carved by the erosion of moving glacier ice over the bedrock below
Landforms built by the deposition of river-borne sediment in the floodplain of a river
questions.solution: Thermokarst: alases (depressions), baydzherakhs (soil pedestals). Climate warming.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes piping, the conditions that promote it, and its consequence in wind-deposited silt?
options: Uniform removal of a thin layer of soil by unchannelled surface water flow during heavy rainfall
Erosion of deep channels in the surface of the soil by running water during flood events
Removal of material across the surface of the ground by flowing water at the surface of the land during heavy storms
Subsurface erosion (tunnel erosion) in wind-deposited silt. Vertical permeability → collapse
questions.solution: Loess: metastable structure. Piping: rapid erosion along preferential flow paths.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which option correctly describes a barrier island, its lagoon and the inlets that cut through it?
options: Island of resistant bedrock rising steeply above the sea surface offshore from the coast
Island built by volcanic eruptions on the sea floor near the coastline of the mainland
Long, narrow sand island parallel to coast. Lagoon behind. Inlet cuts
Sand ridge attached to the mainland coast at one of its two ends
questions.solution: Barrier: wave-dominated. Dune ridge, beach, washover fans. Sea-level rise → barrier transgression.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A functioning GIS needs hardware, software, data, people, and methods, with spatial data stored in which two main forms?
options: The physical computers and the GIS software packages, since the data and the people are not counted as components of a GIS
Only the hardware, software and methods used, without the data and people
Hardware, software, data, people, methods. Spatial data: raster (grid) and vector (points, lines, polygons)
Only the data and the people who manage, update and use the system
questions.solution: GIS: capture, store, analyze, display spatial data. ArcGIS, QGIS.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What engineering problem does phyllite pose due to its smooth cleavage planes?
options: Massive rock with high strength in every direction and no planes
Excellent foundation rock with very high bearing capacity
Ideal aggregate with high resistance to weathering and slaking
Smooth cleavage planes → low friction. Slake-prone
questions.solution: Phyllite: foliated, anisotropic. Weak along cleavage. Weeps along foliation planes.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Isotope ratios: εNd positive = depleted mantle source. εNd negative =:
options: Depleted mantle source that has lost incompatible elements
Primitive undifferentiated mantle of chondritic composition
Source that provides no information about magma provenance
Enriched mantle or continental crustal source
questions.solution: εNd = ((¹⁴³Nd/¹⁴⁴Nd)_sample/(¹⁴⁴Nd/¹⁴⁴Nd)_CHUR - 1) × 10⁴. Positive: depleted. Negative: enriched/crustal.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the nature and tectonic setting of the Closepet Granite batholith in southern India?
options: Early Archean (3.4 Ga) supracrustal belt within the Sargur greenstone sequence
Granite batholith between E and W Dharwar Cratons. ~2.5 Ga. Late Archean
Proterozoic (~1.8 Ga) platform carbonate sequence of the Cuddapah basin
Paleozoic (Permian) coal-bearing rift fill of the Gondwana basins of India
questions.solution: Closepet: N-S trending. High-K, calc-alkaline. Anatectic origin. Mantle+crustal source.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Provenance analysis — heavy mineral assemblage:
options: Ultra-stable (zircon, tourmaline, rutile) vs metastable (garnet, staurolite, kyanite)
Only ultra-stable minerals such as zircon survive, with all others destroyed during transport
Only metastable minerals such as garnet are present, indicating an extremely mature sediment
Only opaque minerals like magnetite and ilmenite are used in provenance determination
questions.solution: ZTR index (zircon-tourmaline-rutile): high = mature, recycled sediment.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A metamorphic facies represents a set of rocks that equilibrated under which controlling condition?
options: P-T conditions: Zeolite, Greenschist, Amphibolite, Granulite, Blueschist, Eclogite
Rock types such as slate, phyllite, schist and gneiss formed in major orogenic belts
Relative geological age of the metamorphic event within the regional metamorphic terrane
The distance of a rock sample from the nearest mapped igneous intrusive body on the surface
questions.solution: Barrovian: greenschist→amphibolite→granulite (increasing T). Blueschist: high P/low T.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A P-wave travels at 8 km/s and arrives 20 s after the earthquake. The (approx.) distance to the source is:
questions.solution: distance = velocity × time = 8×20 = 160 km.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What distinguishes stratabound ore deposits from stratiform ore deposits?
options: Both terms mean the same thing and are used interchangeably in ore geology
Stratabound ore deposits are always syngenetic with the enclosing sedimentary beds that contain them
Stratabound: confined to specific horizon. Stratiform: bedding-parallel, syngenetic
Stratiform ores are always epigenetic, cutting across the sedimentary bedding
questions.solution: Stratabound: epigenetic but stratigraphically controlled. Stratiform: syngenetic, within bedding.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Sm-Nd dating, based on ¹⁴⁷Sm→¹⁴³Nd decay, suits mafic and ultramafic rocks, and εNd values distinguish what?
options: ¹⁴⁷Sm → ¹⁴³Nd (α). T½ = 106 Ga. For mafic/ultramafic, REE minerals. εNd for mantle vs crust
U-Pb method applied to zircon crystals of the same rock body that is being studied in detail
C-14 method applied to organic remains of the recent deposits and overlying sediments
Rb-Sr method applied to whole rocks of the same igneous suite and its various units
questions.solution: Sm-Nd: immobile during alteration/metamorphism. Model ages (T_DM, T_CHUR). Crustal residence.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How are folds classified by interlimb angle, from gentle through to isoclinal folds?
options: Open (0-30°), Close (30-60°), Tight (60-90°), Isoclinal folds with 90° interlimb angle
questions.solution: Interlimb angle: <30° tight, 0° isoclinal (parallel limbs).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal seam covers 2 km², is 3 m thick, with density 1.3 t/m³. The in-situ reserve is about:
questions.solution: Reserve = area×thickness×density = 2×10⁶ m²×3 m×1.3 t/m³ ≈ 7.8 Mt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Groundwater recharge can be estimated by which of the following methods?
options: Only the measurement of the total annual rainfall received by the region concerned during the year
Water table fluctuation, chloride mass balance, baseflow separation, isotope tracers
Only the results of a single pumping test that is carried out on the aquifer under study within the region
Only the pan evaporation data that is collected from the nearby weather station on each day of the year
questions.solution: Recharge: critical for resource assessment. WTF: ΔS = S_y·ΔH. Chloride: P·Cl_p = R·Cl_gw.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What streak colour does the mineral chalcopyrite produce when rubbed on a streak plate?
questions.solution: Chalcopyrite (CuFeS2) — brassy yellow. Most important copper ore mineral.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Fold-thrust belts and isostatic uplift developed along convergent plate boundaries together represent which process?
options: Mountain building occurs without any uplift of the crust at all
Mountains form along transform plate boundaries only where plates slide past each other
Convergent plate boundaries. Fold-thrust belts. Isostatic uplift
Mountains form along divergent plate boundaries only where plates move apart
questions.solution: Orogeny: collision (Himalaya), Andean (subduction), accretional (terranes).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which remote sensing region measures emissivity and temperature and is used for fire detection and urban heat island studies?
options: Emissivity and temperature. Night imaging. Fire detection. Urban heat island
The reflected solar radiation in the visible and near-infrared wavelengths of the spectrum
Laser pulses transmitted by the sensor and reflected back from the ground surface
Natural microwave emissions coming from the Earth's surface
questions.solution: TIR: 8-14 μm atmospheric window. Land surface temperature. Emissivity correction needed.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Tunnel boring machine (TBM) selection depends on:
options: Only the uniaxial compressive strength of the intact rock material
Only the amount of water inflow expected in the tunnel heading
Only the abrasiveness of the rock as measured by the CAI index
Rock mass strength, abrasivity, discontinuities, water inflow
questions.solution: TBM: hard rock (open), soft ground (shielded), mixed face (hybrid). CAI abrasivity index important.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which rocks are formed from volcanic ejecta such as ash, lapilli, bombs, and blocks?
options: Formed from volcanic ejecta (ash, lapilli, bombs, blocks)
Plutonic rocks crystallised slowly at depth from granitic magma
Metamorphic rocks produced by regional high-pressure metamorphism
Lava flows that solidify into massive aphanitic or glassy bodies
questions.solution: Tuff (ash), lapillistone, agglomerate (bombs). Welded tuff = ignimbrite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the likely cause of the Ordovician-Silurian mass extinction about 443 million years ago?
options: Permian-Triassic event with the Siberian Traps and oceanic anoxia (96% loss)
Triassic-Jurassic event linked to CAMP volcanism and Pangaea breakup (76%)
~443 Ma. 85% of species lost. Gondwana glaciation. Sea level drop
K-Pg event with the Chicxulub impact and Deccan volcanism removing the dinosaurs
questions.solution: End-Ordovician: two pulses. Hirnantian glaciation. Major effect on marine life.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How is a conglomerate distinguished from a breccia by the shape of its gravel-sized clasts?
options: Clay-sized clasts (<1/256 mm) in a coarse sand matrix
Sand-sized quartz grains in a fine clay matrix with no larger clasts
Angular gravel-sized clasts, indicating very short transport distance
questions.solution: Conglomerate: high energy environment (rivers, alluvial fans).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Shock metamorphism, caused by meteorite impact, is recognized by the presence of which high-pressure minerals?
options: Regional metamorphism across an entire convergent orogenic belt
Meteorite impact. Very high P (GPa). Coesite, stishovite
Contact metamorphism in the aureole of a large pluton
Seafloor metamorphism by hot circulating hydrothermal fluids
questions.solution: Shock: impact craters. Shatter cones, planar deformation features in quartz.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In the magnetic method, aeromagnetic total intensity data are reduced to pole (RTP), and magnetic anomalies arise from:
options: Ground gravity profiling with complete Bouguer and terrain corrections applied to the data
Seismic reflection imaging using CMP stacking and migration of reflected P-waves
Aeromagnetic survey. Reduce to pole (RTP). Magnetic anomalies from susceptibility contrasts
Vertical electrical sounding interpreted as a layered resistivity model of the subsurface ground
questions.solution: Magnetic: iron-bearing rocks. IGRF correction. Diurnal variation. Mag: survey: nT precision.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Massive sulfide deposits typically contain:
options: Fe, Mn, Al, Si, Ca, Ti
questions.solution: VMS: formed at seafloor hydrothermal vents.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Re-Os dating of molybdenite is a direct dating method because rhenium substitutes for molybdenum; the decay involved is:
options: Direct dating of mineral. Re substitutes for Mo. ¹⁸⁷Re → ¹⁸⁷Os
Indirect method requiring a whole-rock isochron to be constructed
Not useful for dating hydrothermal vein and porphyry deposits
Requires separation of clay mineral fractions from the host rock
questions.solution: Molybdenite Re-Os: in-situ dating. No initial Os (Re/Os very high). Direct age of mineralization.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The angle that a bed makes with the horizontal, measured perpendicular to strike, is the:
questions.solution: Dip is the maximum inclination of a plane; strike is the horizontal line on it.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An aquifer (K = 50 m/day) of cross-section 500 m² has a hydraulic gradient of 0.01. The groundwater discharge is about:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In a sinuous river bend, erosion on the outside cut bank and deposition on the inside point bar together produce what result?
options: Sinuous river bends. Cut bank (outside, erosion) + point bar (inside, deposition)
River channels that remain perfectly straight with no bends at all along their entire length
Sediment body deposited where a river enters a lake or sea and spreads out over the bed
Multiple unstable channels separated by bars of sediment that shift position frequently during floods
questions.solution: Meander: sinuosity > 1.5. Oxbow lake: cut-off meander. Neck cutoff.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How does probabilistic seismic hazard analysis (PSHA) differ from deterministic (DSHA)?
options: Both methods assume a single design earthquake and produce identical results for the site under any condition
PSHA uses only one fault while DSHA considers all possible seismic sources
DSHA is probabilistic in approach and PSHA is deterministic in all cases always
PSHA: probabilistic, all sources, annual probability. DSHA: deterministic, design earthquake
questions.solution: PSHA: hazard curves, return periods, exceedance probability. DSHA: single design earthquake.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A buried erosion surface separating older from much younger rocks is a(n):
options: Plane of maximum curvature along the crest of an anticlinal fold
Surface of continuous deposition with no gap in the geologic record
Fracture along which displacement has occurred between the two blocks
questions.solution: An unconformity represents a gap (missing time) in the rock record.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Blueschist, formed under high pressure and low temperature, contains which diagnostic minerals?
options: High T, low P. Typical of shallow contact metamorphism
Low P, low T. Equivalent to the zeolite facies near surface
High T, high P. Deep crustal metamorphism in granulite facies
High P, low T. Glaucophane + lawsonite + jadeite
questions.solution: Blueschist: subduction zone metamorphism. Contains blue amphibole (glaucophane).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A 3 m seam over 2 km² (density 1.4 t/m³) has a recovery factor of 0.85. The mineable reserve is about:
questions.solution: Mineable = area×thickness×density×recovery = 2M m²×3×1.4×0.85 ≈ 7.1 Mt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes alluvial architecture and the property of the deposits that controls fluid flow?
options: Alluvial deposits consist only of channel sand and gravel deposits in the river valley floor
Alluvial deposits are homogeneous in nature with no internal structure at all whatsoever
Alluvial deposits consist only of overbank mud deposits in the floodplain area
Channel (sand/gravel) and overbank (mud) deposits. Connectivity affects flow
questions.solution: Channel: multistory, multilateral. Overbank: levees, crevasse splays, floodbasin. Heterogeneity.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The law of superposition reliably gives relative age only when the strata are:
options: Always vertical in attitude, since horizontal beds give no age information at all
Igneous intrusions, because only intrusive bodies preserve the true order of emplacement
Strongly folded and overturned by thrusting so that young beds lie on top of old
questions.solution: Tectonic overturning can invert beds, so superposition needs an undisturbed (right-way-up) sequence.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Borehole geophysics: electromagnetic induction log measures:
options: The temperature profile along the entire depth of the borehole
Natural gamma radiation emitted by the rock formations
The porosity of the formation from the density log data
questions.solution: EM induction: no electrode contact. Works in non-conductive mud, air-filled holes.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which igneous rock is composed of more than 90% plagioclase with less than 10% mafic minerals?
options: Rock containing more than ninety percent olivine and pyroxene
Rock containing more than ninety percent pyroxene and hornblende
Rock containing more than ninety percent quartz and alkali feldspar
questions.solution: Anorthosite: plagioclase-rich. Lunar highlands. Economic: Ti, Fe-Ti oxides.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An aquifer (K = 10 m/day) of cross-section 500 m² has a hydraulic gradient of 0.02. The groundwater discharge is about:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: TAS diagram for volcanic rocks: plots total alkali (Na₂O+K₂O) vs silica (SiO₂). Basalt field:
options: Silica less than forty five percent with alkali exceeding five percent
Silica in the range 52-57 percent with alkali less than about five
Silica greater than sixty nine percent and alkali below one percent
questions.solution: TAS: Le Bas et al. (1986). Basalt: 45-52% SiO₂. Andesite: 52-57%. Dacite: 63-69%. Rhyolite: >69%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In the Standard Penetration Test, the N-value is defined as the number of blows per:
options: N-value is the number of blows required for the last 100 mm of penetration
SPT is used only in intact hard rock to measure the rock quality
The test measures permeability by observing water level recovery
N-value: blows per 300mm. Correlated with strength (cohesionless soils)
questions.solution: SPT: 63.5kg hammer, 760mm drop. N₁(60): corrected for energy and overburden.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What term describes a highly non-cylindrical fold, resembling a knife sheath, that forms during intense shear deformation?
options: A perfectly cylindrical fold with a straight hinge line and no change along the axis
Highly non-cylindrical. Like a knife sheath. Intense shear deformation
An open fold with a rounded hinge produced by gentle flexural slip folding
A chevron fold with straight limbs and a sharp angular hinge line
questions.solution: Sheath fold: sheath-like, eye-shaped in cross-section. Ductile shear zones.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A mineral specimen of mass 54 g has a volume of 30 cm³. Its specific gravity is about:
questions.solution: SG = mass/volume = 54/30 = 1.8.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which property of the feldspathoid mineral nepheline distinguishes it from the feldspars?
options: Contains essential quartz in its silica-saturated composition
Framework silicate always coexisting with free quartz
Silica-rich mineral found only in granitic pegmatites
questions.solution: Nepheline: in silica-undersaturated rocks. Associated with alkali feldspar.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 5% moisture, 35% volatile matter and 20% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
questions.solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (5+35+20) = 40%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What do drag folds formed adjacent to a fault indicate about the fault movement?
options: Folding that develops regionally far away from any fault zone during mountain building
Folds formed by the lateral spreading of salt diapirs under their own body weight
A type of fold produced by volcanic intrusion that shows no relation to fault motion
Folding adjacent to fault due to drag. Folds indicate relative motion
questions.solution: Drag fold: in fault zone. Normal drag vs reverse drag (antithetic). Help determine slip sense.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A mineral specimen of mass 105 g has a volume of 20 cm³. Its specific gravity is about:
questions.solution: SG = mass/volume = 105/20 = 5.25.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A tracer test is conducted in the field to determine groundwater velocity and which other transport parameters?
options: Only the direction of flow of the groundwater in the aquifer
Only the depth to the water table at the injection point
Only the total thickness of the aquifer at the test site
questions.solution: Tracer: inject and monitor. Determines velocity, dispersivity.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which measurable parameters are commonly used as indicators of coal rank?
options: Only the ash content determined by combustion of a representative coal sample
Only the moisture content of the coal as-mined from the seam in the field
Vitrinite reflectance (Ro%), calorific value, volatile matter, carbon content
Only the sulphur content of the coal seam as determined by chemical methods
questions.solution: Ro% is most reliable. ASTM: uses Btu/lb and VM for classification. ISO: Ro%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An opencast block of 20000 m² has 20 m of overburden above the seam. The overburden volume to be removed is:
questions.solution: Volume = area × depth = 20000×20 = 400000 m³ = 0.4 million m³.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Molluscan shells are composed of which carbonate minerals, and which mineral group is generally absent?
options: Shells are predominantly composed of silica (opal), with calcite restricted to the hinge region
All shells are built of pure calcite, and aragonite never occurs in any mollusc group
Aragonite (most), calcite (some), both (some). Not silica (except in diatoms)
Shell mineralogy is fixed within each class and never mixes calcite with aragonite layers
questions.solution: Molluscs: aragonite common. Bivalves: aragonite or calcite. Gastropods: aragonite. Cephalopods: aragonite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which spaceborne sensor carries OLI and TIRS instruments and has a 16-day revisit and a 185 km swath?
options: Landsat 8: OLI (9 bands, 30m) + TIRS (2 thermal, 100m). 16-day revisit. 185km swath
Landsat 8: carries only a single panchromatic band at 15m, and has no thermal capability
Landsat 8: 36 spectral bands at 250m resolution, offering a daily revisit period
Landsat 8: 13 bands, 10m resolution, a 5-day revisit period and a 290km swath
questions.solution: Landsat: 1972-2023. OLI bands: coastal, blue, green, red, NIR, SWIR1, SWIR2, pan (15m), cirrus.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the geological age, coal-bearing nature, and importance of the Barakar Formation?
options: Triassic marine limestone with abundant ammonite and brachiopod faunas
Cretaceous deltaic sandstone with thick lignite seams in the coastal belt
Permian coal measures in Gondwana. Major coal seams. Mineral matter low
Jurassic conglomerate and lava flows marking a major rift episode in the basin
questions.solution: Barakar: most important coal-bearing formation in India. Raniganj Formation also coal-bearing.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In groundwater geophysics, the nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) method is notable because it can do what?
options: Seismic refraction profiles used for mapping the depth to the top of the bedrock
Resistivity sounding curves interpreted as a one dimensional layered earth model of the subsurface geology
Nuclear magnetic resonance (MRS). Direct detection of groundwater. T₂* decay time for pore size
Gravity gradient survey used for locating deep seated basement density contrasts
questions.solution: MRS: surface NMR. Water content ε, decay T₂*. Logging NMR also. Porosity + permeability estimate.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which structural feature describes linear fabric elements such as mineral alignment, intersection or stretching in rocks?
options: A planar fabric element defined by the preferred orientation of platy minerals
A surface of fracture with no measurable displacement, dividing the rock into blocks
Linear fabric element (mineral alignment, intersection, stretching)
A large-scale fold structure formed by regional horizontal compressive stress
questions.solution: Lineation: parallel to fold axes, mineral elongation, or intersection of foliations.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A rock retains 25% of its original parent isotope (half-life 0.7 Gyr). Its radiometric age is about:
questions.solution: 25% remaining ⇒ 2 half-lives ⇒ age = 2×0.7 = 1.4 Gyr.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Metamorphic facies series: Barrovian type:
options: Low-pressure/high-temperature gradient typical of shallow contact metamorphism
Very high-pressure gradient producing blueschist and eclogite facies rocks
Medium P/T gradient (typical of continental collision). Kyanite → sillimanite
High-temperature/low-pressure gradient typical of magmatic arc and rift settings worldwide
questions.solution: Barrovian: clockwise P-T path. Kyanite → sillimanite. Buchan: andalusite → sillimanite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A migmatite is a partially melted metamorphic rock showing which characteristic banding?
options: Fully melted rock that crystallized into a coarse-grained granite
Sedimentary rock that recrystallized entirely in the solid state with no melt phase involved
Unmelted protolith that retained its original sedimentary layering
Partially melted metamorphic rock. Dark (restite) + light (leucosome) bands
questions.solution: Migmatite: between metamorphism and igneous. Leucosome: granitic melt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Amphibolite, the medium-to-high-grade equivalent of basalt or gabbro, consists mainly of which minerals?
options: Chlorite + epidote + albite + actinolite. Low-grade equivalent of basalt
Hornblende + plagioclase. Medium-high grade. Equivalent to basalt/gabbro
Pyroxene + garnet + feldspar. High-grade anhydrous equivalent of basalt
Glaucophane + lawsonite + jadeite. High-pressure equivalent of basalt
questions.solution: Amphibolite: medium to high grade (amphibolite facies). No pyroxene (granulite has pyroxene).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal seam covers 1 km², is 5 m thick, with density 1.3 t/m³. The in-situ reserve is about:
questions.solution: Reserve = area×thickness×density = 1×10⁶ m²×5 m×1.3 t/m³ ≈ 6.5 Mt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Remote sensing of mineralogy: ASTER bands for hydrothermal alteration:
options: SWIR bands (5,6,7,8) for clay, carbonate, sericite
VNIR bands (1,2,3) for iron oxide and hematite mapping
TIR bands (10-14) for iron and manganese oxides only
Single SWIR band 8 for all alteration minerals
questions.solution: ASTER SWIR: clay (band 6), carbonate (band 8), alunite (band 5). OH absorption features.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Rock mass rating (RMR): RMR = UCS+RQD+spacing+condition+groundwater. For granite with UCS=120MPa, RQD=80%, spacing=1m:
questions.solution: UCS=120→12, RQD=80→18, spacing=1m→20, condition→20, GW→15. Total ~85. Depends on exact ratings.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Metamorphic rocks are formed by the action of which agents on pre-existing rocks?
options: Evaporation and precipitation of dissolved salts from sea water
Rapid cooling of molten lava at the Earth's surface
Heat and/or pressure on pre-existing rocks
Cementation and compaction of transported detrital grains
questions.solution: Metamorphism alters mineralogy and texture in the solid state under heat/pressure.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An aquifer has hydraulic conductivity 10 m/day and a hydraulic gradient of 0.05. The Darcy velocity is:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In the seismic reflection method, subsurface structure is imaged using which waves and processing steps such as CMP stacking and migration?
options: Mapping of the subsurface using critically refracted first arrivals at long offsets
Determination of the water table using direct current injected through steel electrodes
Estimation of rock density contrasts from measurement of the Earth's gravity field at the surface
Subsurface imaging by reflected P-waves. CMP stacking, migration. Resolution: λ/4 (~20m at 50 Hz)
questions.solution: Reflection: petroleum exploration. 2D, 3D seismic. Vibroseis (land), airgun (marine).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Rock bolt installation: grouted rock bolts provide:
options: Active prestressing applied immediately at the time of installation
Surface support that holds only the loose skin of the excavation
No reinforcement until the bolt is re-tensioned after grouting
Passive reinforcement (tension develops as rock moves)
questions.solution: Grouted bolts: resin or cement. Passive: load develops with rock movement. Full column grouting.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What event does the term 'Cambrian explosion' describe in the history of life?
options: Triassic recovery of fauna after the great end-Permian mass extinction event
Precambrian radiation of soft-bodied Ediacaran organisms in the Vendian
Permian diversification of reptiles across the supercontinent Pangaea
Rapid appearance of major animal phyla (~541 Ma). Burgess Shale (507 Ma)
questions.solution: Burgess Shale (Canadian Rockies): exceptional preservation (soft parts). Trilobites, brachiopods.
